reason: The protocol tested factor-base shape. It did not test the dual question: can a cheap statistic of the TARGET select high-yield targets? The counting identity fixes the mean of r over all targets but says nothing about conditioning, and conditioning is nearly free in relative cost (a selector costs ~1e3 ns, one trial costs |F|^ceil(m/2) lookups), so even a 1% lift would be a 1% speedup of the relation phase. Declared after the fact; reported as post hoc.

addedHypothesis.claim: Some statistic phi(R) costing at most a few hundred arithmetic cycles predicts r(R) well enough to raise relations per trial at production |F|.

design.data: exact r(R) for every R in E (ecell dump mode), both rungs, three shapes, m in {2,3}; no sampling
design.statistics: x < p/2; v2(x); x mod 3; x mod 5; Legendre(x); floor(log2 x); rational height h(x) = min B with x = a/b, |a|,|b| <= B (EEA, computed in heights.c)
design.null: analytic: under exchangeability of r across targets, a bucket of size n_b has sd = sqrt(sigma^2 (1 - n_b/N)/n_b), so z is exact without resampling; Sidak correction over the buckets tested
design.operational_metric: cost per relation = [(c_gen + c_sel)/f + c_trial] / (lift * mu); a selector wins iff the search term stays below c_trial

addedHypothesis.killLine: If every non-degenerate bucket has (c_gen+c_sel)/f >> c_trial at production, target selection is not a lever regardless of the lift.
addedHypothesis.prediction: The rational-height statistic separates r, but only through the degenerate case R in F and its first ring; no cheap statistic is a lever.
